owner_and_capability: Scheduler Runtime — the Worker application in services/scheduler (scheduler-runtime/application), contract step for #2746: the scheduler opens its transactions through a consumer-owned TenantRuntime port bound by modules/schedulerruntime/jobruntime, reads its settings keys as its own constants behind a registry guard of the root, publishes the overdue events through Delivery's realtimeevents, and reaches the retained repositories and services only through ports the root binds
atomic_cutover: One code-only change: services/scheduler drops its imports of cmp, internal/timezone, models/audit, models/config, models/facilities, models/schedule, models/users, realtime, services/config, services/users, tenant and bun in production and of every listed target in its internal suites. It opens its transactions through the consumer-owned TenantRuntime port (Attach, WithinTenant, WithinTenantRetry, WithinAdmin, WithCommitGuard, RegisterAfterCommit in plain values), which the new modules/schedulerruntime/jobruntime (scheduler-runtime/postgres, covered by the existing tenant-runtime rule) binds; WorkerDependencies loses DB and takes the port, TenantCommand takes the school as int64. Calendar values come from sharedkernel/calendar. The settings keys and the end-of-day clear mode are the scheduler's own constants with the semantics of the former Resolve*OrDefault helpers; the root refuses a Worker whose key the registry does not define or defines as a secret (modules/settings/compose.VerifyPreloadKeys) and binds the minute snapshot to the Settings Platform's cross-tenant read through compose.NewTenantSnapshots as an optional SettingsSnapshotSource of the existing SettingsResolver port, so no field or setter is added; a snapshot the source did not resolve fails the school's tick instead of falling back to database reads. The overdue tick publishes through two new Delivery producers in realtimeevents and reads the day's blocks and existing rooms through DayInstanceReader and ExistingRoomReader; the booking audit, the student lifecycle (statuses as stored values, IDs instead of models), the status audit, the change-history sweep and the slot checkout closing are scheduler ports. api/scheduler_ports.go binds them to the retained repositories and services without importing their packages: named string types are converted through small generic helpers. The internal suites compose through test support (testpkg.PassthroughTenantRuntime, ScriptedTenantRuntime, TenantIDFromContext, WithinAdminTransaction, RegisterAfterCommit) and record what the scheduler asks of its ports. The further keys of the issue text (models/active, models/platform, services/active, services/enrollment, services/notifications, services/pwa, services/reminders, services/schedule, services/staffmessaging, database/repositories/active, database/repositories/platform, database/repositories/schedule and internal_test bun) were already absent at the base and are not claimed here. No separate provider remained to delete: the scheduler reached the retained packages through direct imports, which this change removes; the removed symbols WorkerDependencies.DB, Scheduler.db, Scheduler.tenantRuntimeConfigured, tenantRuntimeValue and schedulerSettingsBatchResolver have zero callers (go build ./... and a repository-wide search).
tests: services/scheduler: all 317 top-level tests pass against the isolated PostgreSQL test database (318 test functions including TestMain, 312 before). The suites that drove the legacy repositories (overdue tick, status-flag clear, session-end pass, PWA usage, change-history sweep, activate-students, booking audit) now pin what the scheduler asks of its ports: the calls, their arguments, the tenant transaction they run in, mode and time gating, rollback and day marking. They no longer exercise the repositories' SQL; the SQL sides are pinned where they live (below and in modules/careplan/internal/adapters/postgres, database/repositories/pwausage, services/users). The rollover rollback test still writes and rolls back a real row through the production tenant runtime.
